title: Understanding the Forces
text: To find the ratio of the centripetal force to the child's weight, you need to calculate both forces separately. The centripetal force is given by the formula: $$F_{c}=mv**{2}/r$$, $$where$$ $$\, \text{m$$} $$is$$ $$the$$ $$mass$$, $$v$$ is the velocity, and $$r$$ is the radius. The weight is given by $$W=mg$$, $$where$$ $$g$$ is the acceleration due to gravity.

title: Calculate the Centripetal Force
text: First, convert the rotational speed from revolutions per minute to meters per second. Use the formula: v=2*pi*r*(revolutions per second).

title: Calculate the Weight
text: The weight of the child can be calculated using the formula: $$W=mg$$, $$where$$ $$\, \text{m$$} $$is$$ $$the$$ $$mass$$ $$of$$ $$the$$ $$child$$ $$and$$ $$g$$ is the acceleration due to gravity (approximately $$9.8\,\tfrac{\text{m}}{\text{s}**2}$$).

title: Find the Ratio
text: Now, find the ratio of the centripetal force to the weight using the formula: Ratio=$$F_{c}$$/W.
